doc.title: John Pizzarelli interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, October 18, 2023 [interview 2 of 2]

title: Chord charts and letting the band find the figures
summary: His charts are chord charts, with recordings for the shout choruses. He prefers arrangements to happen organically, starting and ending together.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Are your charts chord charts with cues for riffs and breaks and that kind of thing?

No they’re just chord charts and then I’ll send them the record so I said you know, “You’ll see where the shout chorus is.” And to me that’s the funny part is like I like the guy to learn the tunes and if like when Isaiah joined the band I was like, “Okay, you learned the Nat Cole stuff, great, that’s something.” But when we do, I’m not a stickler for like, “Hey we’re going to all do this.” I like it to sort of organically happen, to say like, you know, “Be on the lookout, I may play a figure we could all play it together.” You hear it, you’ll play it. And that part’s sort of fun. I like to just have the harmonies in the beginning, you know, know how we’re going to start and finish. You know the ending might be nice.
